ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: pilgrims, scholars, the enclave and the river folk
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Four more peoples of peaceful callings: a fellowship of pilgrims who walk between the shrines and keep hostels, a learned society that keeps an archive and trades in books, a spacer enclave of brokers between the towns and the ships above, and river folk who fish and run the ferries. Each has its own gear, colours, faith, towns and words, and comes to the colony's gate in its own way.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: They are among the world's peoples when a new world is made, once each, at the game's usual chances; remove them in the world's faction list like any other people. A save made before them meets them when one of them arises during play.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: All four are mostly peaceful. They defend their towns, and they raid only when the colony has turned them hostile, by the game's own rules, and seldom then. Their notables have titles of their own, their messengers words of their own, and their towns a plan of their own when the land suits it.

li.heading: Who they are

table.li: People | Lives by | Age | On the map | Their towns

The pilgrim fellowship | Walking between holy places | Medieval | Cloaks dyed sage, wide cone hats; wardens of the way in one kit with spears | Few: a shrine's court with its flame, and a hostel of bedrolls
The learned society | Books and what is known | Industrial | Claret coats and gowns of every cut; proctors in flak and claret | Few: archives with a reading hall and stacks
The spacer enclave | Trade between the towns and the ships above | Spacer | Pale cyan coats; marshals in one issue of recon armour and charge rifle | Fewest: a market round a landing pad
The river folk | Fishing and the ferries | Medieval | Kingfisher blue hats and coats; river wardens in one kit with fishing spears | Landings on a river bank, with docks out over the water

li.after: With Ideology each keeps a faith of its own (the pilgrim's way, the open book, the exchange, the river's keeping) and its own style; with Biotech each has a share of other kinds of people. With Vanilla Ideology Expanded's memes or Alpha Memes their faiths take a meme of nomads, of the monastic life, of trade and of machines doing the work, or of water and of the stranger carried across too; the pilgrims' may be of Vanilla Ideology Expanded's omnism and the society's of its agnosticism.

li.heading: Where their ways began
li.text: Each keeps a founding story, a few sayings, and what it honours and fears, shown on their card and spoken in their letters, messengers, visitors and talk, as release A's peoples' are.

points.li: The pilgrim fellowship began with Old Brannoc, a nearly blind preacher turned out of his town for praying at the wrong shrine, who set out with a boy to lead him to every holy place he had heard of and blessed every door he came to at dusk, whether it opened or not. A pilgrim carries a shell for every shrine reached. They say "peace on this house" and "there is no last shrine"; they honour the open door and the old shrines, and fear the shut door and sitting still too long.

The learned society began the night the old archive at Hesk burned and a clerk named Ilse Varro carried out eleven books and a ledger in a handcart, and spent her life copying them. Every year on the night of the fire the fellows argue until dawn about what was lost. They say "nothing known should be lost" and "copy it twice"; they honour the copied page and a good question, and fear fire and the closed mind.

The spacer enclave began with the crew of an ore hauler that came down with a dead drive. Its purser, Ines Okoro, sold its cargo, passage and debts one bargain at a time until the crew owned a landing pad and the ships above were calling, and every bargain since is in the hauler's manifest. They say "a bargain struck is kept to the last digit" and "terms first, then talk"; they honour the kept bargain and the body made better, and fear the default and being stranded.

The river folk began the night the dam broke and the valley towns drowned, when the ferrywoman Wenna Reed's boats pulled people off the rooftops for three days and those they carried stayed. They tie a knot in the net for everyone pulled from the water. They say "take what the water gives and no more" and "carry the stranger across"; they honour clean water and the stranger carried across, and fear fouled water and the river rising.

li.heading: What they wear, carry and know
li.text: As with the league, the order and the herders, no two of them look alike: each people wears its colour on a piece or two, its soldiers one kit, its civilians whatever their age and calling would, from the game, the DLCs and the mods loaded, and the base game alone dresses and arms every one of them. Pawns already in a game keep what they have.

points.li: The pilgrim fellowship: every pilgrim in a travelling cloak dyed sage, a cape, a robe or a mantle, the cone hat over it, prayer beads, now and then a pack or a banner; the keeper in a bishop's mitre; the wardens of the way in one kit of helmet and sage cape with spears or pikes; the archers with quivers and a wide hat or a headscarf. They carry a book of the road or herbs, candles for the shrines, now and then a map. A few are wanderers, minstrels or monks of A RimWorld of Magic, a few wardens paladins and archers rangers, and their keeper is often a priest.

The learned society: fellows and scholars in a claret gown or coat of any cut over a collar shirt, now and then a skullcap, carrying textbooks, novels, schematics or a map; the proctors in one kit of flak under the claret jacket and a military cap, with guns and, where Vanilla Weapons Expanded's Non-Lethal set is loaded, tasers, dart guns and stun batons. A few are arcanists, enchanters or chronomancers of A RimWorld of Magic, a few have a psylink (Royalty), on a chronopath's or an empath's path with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded, and a few scholars had the quick study gene put in (Biotech).

The spacer enclave: hands, factors and the chair in pale cyan coats over industrial clothes or spacer unisuits, with data glasses, tool belts and packs, the chair now and then in psychic finery; the marshals in one issue of recon armour in the enclave's colour over a spacer bodysuit, with a charge weapon or a smart rifle. Hands carry components, chemfuel or medicine. Many of the chairs and some factors and marshals have a psylink, on a harmonist's, empath's, skipmaster's, protector's or warlord's path with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded; a few hands are technomancers and a few marshals psionics; a few had a gene put in, strong immunity, fast healing, good looks or a long life.

The river folk: kingfisher blue on their floppy hats, tuques and coats, the rest their own; the river wardens in one kit of blue tuque and plain clothes with fishing spears; fishers with slings, throwing stones and javelins, archers with quivers. They carry net cloth, herbs or timber, the fishers the day's catch or fish sauce. Their river master is often a druid, a few wardens and archers rangers.

With A RimWorld of Magic a caster among them looks like one: the pilgrims' wandering mages in the wanderer's cloak, their monks and their keeper, when a priest, in a disciple hood, their wardens' paladins in the Helm of the Valiant; the society's arcanists in an arcane hood, its chronomancers and enchanters in a wizard hat; the river folk's druids in a hood of protection. A priest or a paladin among the pilgrims may heal one of the colony's hurt, a river folk's druid cure an infection or a flu. A visitor with a class names their craft to the first of the colony they meet, who remarks on it; a colonist who sees a raider's caster names it too. Their card says what crafts are among them, and their letters mention them now and then. Now and then a visitor who is content, or of a people allied with the colony, casts a helpful spell for it with the mod's own effects, once a visit at most; in a fight they cast by the mod's own AI and settings, its most broken spells kept out. Sparing: a few of a hundred of a kind, a people's head more often.

Their kinds of people (Biotech) are a real mix, and still mostly baseliners: every kind with the pilgrims, anima and gauranlen tree folk, the Avaloi, the forsaken and wood elves among them; genies, high elves, the Avaloi, archons and orangutans with the scholars; starjacks, archons, the Avaloi, lapis, androids, Åskbarns and Uredde in the enclave; coastal merren and now and then an abyssal one, nereids, poluxkin and gauranlenkin among the river folk, each where its mod is loaded.

The pilgrim fellowship: at dusk a band of three to five of them may ask the colony for a night's shelter. Taken in, each sleeps in a warm corner indoors and they go on at first light, their eldest blessing the gate, and the colony is glad of it; one night in ten one of them has brought a cough in off the road, and the one who sat up with them catches it. In a holy year their hostel asks the colony for food. Hungry pilgrims, pilgrims to a relic or an anima tree, the great pilgrimage, the holy year and the prophet on the roads come from them likeliest, and their pilgrims, processions, penitents and mourners camp more often. In the spring and summer, on the fellowship's walking day, a long file of six to nine pilgrims may stop to pray at the colony's graves, or at its gate where it has none: the colony may walk out to the graves with them or see them off to the road, give them food for the road, or watch from the wall. A traveller lost on the wrong road likeliest is a pilgrim.

The learned society: one of their copyists may ask to copy the colony's records for their archive where the colony gathers (a tribal colony's stories, written down), and leave a book in return or teach the colony's best reader while at it. Their caravans carry books, schematics and techprints. A travelling scholar, a book swapper, an old vault opened and the comet come from them likeliest, and their scholars, surveyors and teachers camp more often. Once a year at most, on the society's night of the fire, a fellow may ask to hold a disputation where the colony gathers: that evening the colony gathers to hear the fellow argue with its best mind, who learns from it, or the two sit an hour together instead. A travelling teacher likeliest is theirs.

The spacer enclave: when the colony is industrial or later, their factor may call by radio to ask leave to come down by the gate. Bidden, the factor, two to four marshals and the goods come down by drop pod, trade at the gate, and walk off when they are done. Busy orbital lanes and a ship come down come from them likeliest. In any age their factor may offer salvage from above that isn't worth lifting back to orbit (steel and parts; cloth and medicine for a tribal or medieval colony, plasteel and chemfuel for a later one) for two in five of its worth, by radio or comms, or by a runner on foot to a colony with neither. Bought, it comes down by drop pod by the colony's trade spot and the silver goes to their runner. A tourist likeliest comes by way of their market.

The river folk: a boat-trader may bring a catch of the colony's own waters to the gate, for silver or for food from the stores (with Odyssey, whose fish they are). In the spring they ask for timber for the boats, in the summer cloth for the nets. The flood downriver and the ice road come from them likeliest, and their fishers camp more often. In the spring, summer and fall two or three boatmen may ask to dry and mend their nets on the colony's bank for the day, and leave fish of the colony's waters (with Odyssey) or net cloth for it; the colony's best crafter may learn their knots at their side.

li.heading: Their towns, and new peoples like them

points.li: The river folk's landings stand by a river where the world has one: as a new world starts, a landing the game put where no river runs moves to one within twelve tiles, and with none it stays, its map laid on dry ground. Their landing's map is placed where most of its docks reach the water, and the docks are laid as a jetty over it; with Odyssey its racks hold fish of that water.

The pilgrims' shrine and hostel, the society's archive and the enclave's market are laid out to their plans when a town's map is made, as release A's are; where the land is too wet or rough for it, the game makes its own base.

New peoples that arise during play may take their ways: survivors by a river, and half of them, may become river folk; a band led by a learned one, scholars; a league of spacer-age towns, an enclave; faithful who broke away in an industrial or spacer world, pilgrims. The pace stays as it was.

li.heading: Of their own: gifts, trust and camps

points.li: The pilgrim fellowship: in a holy year or a great pilgrimage two or three of the fellowship may raise a hostel by the road through the colony's land for ten to fifteen days: a long hut of bedrolls, the shrine's flame (a brazier with Royalty, else a torch) and a bread table. Travellers of every people at peace walk in for a night or two and walk on, each with their people's news, and a place their news names is marked as heard of. The hostel asks once for bread each morning, carried out by the colony's people from then on, and invites the colony to the evening blessing, where the cough going round the crowded hut can be caught (the pilgrims' cough, through the harm budget). Two travellers of feuding peoples (never two at war) may quarrel at the fire, at a camp brawl's rate. The hut stays standing when they go.

The learned society: when the colony's map holds an old place (a sealed room of the game's ancient dangers still in the fog, or the land's landmark from Odyssey, Vanilla Landmarks Expanded or Geological Landforms), two fellows ask leave to camp beside it for four days, measuring it by day. Then they say exactly what lies inside, counted from the map itself: sleeping mechanoids by kind, fleshbeasts, hives and the insects round them, ancient caskets and how many hold someone, sealed crates, or nothing at all; and they leave the colony progress on its research. Let open, they break in as they go, and whatever sleeps there wakes, the game's own danger.

The pilgrim fellowship's pilgrimage: a file bound for a shrine in reach (a fellowship town, a town whose faith keeps a relic, an old shrine at a landmark) asks whether anyone of the colony would walk with them, the one with a grief or a guilt to carry likeliest. The one who goes is away ten to thirty days as a caravan of their own, the roads and weather the world's own, and may bring the pilgrims' cough home (through the harm budget). Home, they bring a pilgrim's shell (with Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Relics and Artifacts a token of a relic's shrine too), a lasting memory of the shrine, steadier faith with Ideology, and their heaviest grief or guilt eased; the fellowship gives +6. Once to a colonist, spaced with the other gifts.

The learned society's books kept from the fire: when one of their towns has fallen (a ruin of the region's ledger, not the colony's doing) or a great fire burns near one, a copyist brings a cart of the archive, four to eight books of the game's own (with Vanilla Books Expanded, its papers) and with Anomaly a tome in a sealed crate, and asks the colony to keep them a season. Kept open, the colony's readers may read them; kept locked away, nobody does. Their cart comes back for them: every book there is +8 and one book left with the colony; a book lost or sold, or the tome's seal broken, is a lasting wrong.

The spacer enclave's body made better, on terms: the factor offers one of the colony's people a bionic eye, arm, leg or spine (one missing or scarred first, else the best fighter's arm or leg), or with Alpha Implants one of its animal bionics for a colonist's bonded beast. Paid now, or on terms: a fifth more in all, a fifth of it down and four instalments, one asked for by letter each season and carried to the gate. Their surgeon (Medicine 14 to 18) drops in by pod, or walks in to a tribal colony, and fits it at the colony's medical bed by the game's own surgery, its chance on the card. A missed instalment is a default: goodwill falls, the debt joins the colony's debts in the world's ledger, and no lander or caravan of theirs comes until it is paid in full.

The spacer enclave's pad by the colony: two factors and two marshals rent ground at the colony's edge for ten to fifteen days at an exact figure every five days (or for nothing, as friends), lay a small pad tile by tile beside their stalls, and trade every day, a pod bringing fresh stock down at dawn. They ask the colony to keep its people off the pad, and to sell them ten meals at their worth and a tenth. It can turn: they try to shave the rent (the camps' terms bent), a band of their enemies comes for the stock, or the colony raises the rent by half and they pay or pack up and go.

The river folk's crossing: where a river cuts the colony's map, two or three boatmen lay a crossing over its narrows in a day, a span at a time with a bar each, and plank both banks, with the colony's wood (rope and plank before the industrial age, with Odyssey a heavy bridge on piles after); the colony's builder may work beside them and learn. The crossing is the colony's, and once a year, on their knot night, the boatmen ask to rest at it until morning.
